name: Hurricane Electric

profile.reading: Hurricane Electric Fremont 1 sits at 760 Mission Court, Fremont, California 94539, also the company's own stated corporate headquarters address. Hurricane Electric's own colocation page describes a 45,000 square foot facility with 1,000 cabinets, diverse UPS and generator backup power, 2 internet exchange points (SFMIX and FCIX), 6 carriers with diverse fiber, and connections to 20 internet networks, alongside individually locked cabinets, custom video surveillance, card keyed doors, raised floors, and 24 by 7 by 365 onsite staff and remote hands support. Hurricane Electric, per Wikipedia's own article, was established in 1994 by Mike Leber and operates under autonomous system number 6939, positioning itself as the largest global IP network by network adjacencies in both IPv4 and IPv6 as of June 2024, and the largest global IPv6 network by IPv6 prefixes announced. The company connects to more than 338 major exchange points, peers directly with more than 11,990 networks under an open peering policy requiring no contracts, and maintains more than 55 terabits per second of active public peering capacity and more than 900 terabits per second of private peering capacity. Hurricane Electric also operates a free IPv6 tunnel broker service that, as of June 2024, supported 52,760 provisioned tunnels across 174 countries. The company operates two other colocation facilities already on file elsewhere in this registry, a second Fremont building known as Fremont 2 and a smaller San Jose facility at 55 South Market Street. Fremont sits in the southern San Francisco Bay Area, in Alameda County, a secondary but well established Bay Area colocation and interconnection market that offers lower real estate and power costs than downtown San Francisco or San Jose while remaining close enough to Silicon Valley's dense fiber infrastructure for network operators like Hurricane Electric to maintain the low latency peering relationships central to its business model.

reading:
Hurricane Electric was founded in 1994 by Mike Leber, who remains founder, CEO, owner, and president of the privately held, founder-owned company, headquartered in Fremont, California.

Hurricane Electric is primarily a network operator, running Autonomous System 6939 with peering at more than 330 major exchange points and direct exchange with more than 11,000 other networks. The company describes itself as operating the largest global IPv6 network by IPv6 prefixes announced, with more than 50 terabits per second of active public peering capacity and more than 400 terabits per second of active private peering capacity, alongside an IPv6 tunnel broker service with more than 52,000 provisioned tunnels across 174 countries. Its colocation and hosting facilities are concentrated at three sites, one in San Jose and two in Fremont, California, its home headquarters city.

The registry here tracks 2 Hurricane Electric facilities, both in California, consistent with the company's Fremont and San Jose concentration described on Wikipedia. Like FirstLight and Lumen elsewhere in this registry, Hurricane Electric's data centers exist primarily to support its own network and peering business rather than functioning as a standalone national colocation platform, and its network-density figures, peering capacity in terabits per second, are not directly comparable to the megawatt power figures recorded for hyperscale and wholesale operators elsewhere in this registry.
